findings.claim: Check this if Alaska and Jan 1 work for you: at 42,500 points, it has the lowest point quote among the economy leads shown.
findings.issue: The only other economy lead shown is United Jan 9. The superlative therefore orders different program currencies and is embedded after the colon in a recommendation rationale. The raw counts are correct, but using their order as an advantage is unsupported cross-program economic framing. Conditional Alaska access and Jan 1 fit already provide a sufficient honest research reason.
findings.uncertainty: A strictly literal reading treats lowest point quote only as an accurate count comparison, without a value claim. I judge its position in the check-this rationale to imply an advantage. No explicit cheapest/best-value wording appears. This interpretive boundary is recorded for parent integration; correct cards alone do not resolve it.
findings.recommended_change: Keep the conditional Alaska/Jan 1 research reason and remove the cross-program lowest-point clause. No mandatory replacement comparison or extra card is required.
